learningObjective: Identify factors that can invalidate torch.compile's compilation cache and cause re-compilation.

canonicalClaims.claim: torch.compile's in-memory compile cache is keyed on guard-relevant attributes (shape/stride/dtype/device/requires_grad/etc.) and on the source-code identity of the function; changes to any guarded attribute or a process restart (without a persistent cache) result in fresh compilation.
nonImplications: Does not imply the cache is only in-memory forever; persistent-cache mechanisms exist.
Does not imply the key is limited to (shape, dtype, device, stride); many guards participate.

misconceptions.claim: Matching input metadata still misses the cache.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Matching guarded metadata is a cache hit by design.

misconceptions.claim: torch.compile automatically persists its cache across process restarts by default.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Default behavior is in-memory; persistent-cache is opt-in / experimental in current releases.

misconceptions.claim: Device changes are not part of the cache key.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Device is a guard; changes cause recompile.

misconceptions.claim: The cache key excludes function source; two different functions with the same op sequence share cache entries.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Source identity is part of the cache key.

implementationFacts: Guards: shape, stride, dtype, device, requires_grad, class, source-code identity
Cache serves distinct compiled variants for distinct guard configurations
Persistent-cache mechanisms are being developed but are not the default
performanceScenarios: Cold-start latency in production is often dominated by cache-miss compiles; understanding guard categories helps reduce them.
